profile.campus: Google Council Bluffs, Pottawattamie County, IA
profile.address: Bancroft Street, Google Data Center, Council Bluffs, Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County, IA
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Council Bluffs, Iowa data center campus, mapped along Bancroft Street in Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County. Google's own locations page for Iowa, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Iowa data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the Council Bluffs campus was the site of Google's original $600 million Iowa investment announced in 2007, and that the company has since invested more than $20 billion in the state; in 2025 Google announced a further $7 billion investment shared between an expanded Council Bluffs campus and a new Cedar Rapids facility. Google reports generating $2.7 billion of economic activity for Iowa businesses in 2025 and training over 112,000 Iowans in digital skills through its Grow with Google partnerships.

The Council Bluffs campus has grown into one of Google's largest data center clusters globally over nearly two decades of continuous expansion, though Google's own public materials describe the campus in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

MidAmerican Energy, the principal electric utility serving Council Bluffs, has pursued a long-running commitment to source renewable wind generation for its Iowa customers, a factor Google has cited in its own public materials as part of the state's appeal for data center investment. Iowa's data center-specific sales tax exemption on qualifying equipment and electricity, administered at the state level, has been credited by state economic development officials with helping draw and retain large-scale data center investment in the state, including from Microsoft and Meta, both separately tracked in this registry.

reading.body:
This building lies within Google's Council Bluffs campus in Pottawattamie County, Iowa, one of Google's largest data center clusters globally. Google does not publish individual building capacities within Council Bluffs, and third-party estimates of the entire campus range from 100 to 300+ MW across its full build-out, a range this site does not adopt as fact because Google itself has not confirmed it. The campus began in 2007 with a $600 million initial investment and has expanded continuously; Google announced in 2025 a further $7 billion investment shared between Council Bluffs expansion and a new Cedar Rapids facility, signaling continued growth at this location.

The binding resource for this campus is power from MidAmerican Energy, the principal regional utility. MidAmerican has committed to sourcing renewable wind generation for its Iowa customers, a factor Google has cited as part of the state's appeal for data center siting. Iowa's state-level data tax exemption on data center equipment and electricity has been credited by state economic development officials with drawing and retaining large-scale capacity from Google, Microsoft, and Meta. These factors—renewable grid supply and tax incentive—address two of the three constraints on AI scaling that define this site's thesis: power and financial return on builds.

Among Iowa's 52 mapped data center facilities, only two operators publish megawatt figures; those two facilities total 18 MW published capacity statewide. Council Bluffs ranks third in the state by published MW, though Google's own disclosures do not supply the figure for this individual campus, and independent estimates span a range too wide to guide investment or capacity planning. The lack of operator-published capacity at one of the state's largest AI infrastructure sites represents a gap in the public record available to readers assessing where grid constraints are tightest.
